Hi all — looping in a couple technical details so Priya knows what to expect.

Quick summary of what Redwood can deliver for a tenant-scoped retention / proof-of-delete:
- Default tenant inference telemetry + debug trace TTL: 30 days.
- Session/interaction logs (request/response metadata) are stored in an isolated tenant bucket and can be exported as NDJSON or compressed CSV.
- Proof-of-delete: we produce a manifest CSV with the following columns: tenant_id, object_key, deletion_timestamp_utc, deletion_job_id, deletion_hmac_signature. The manifest is signed by our Compliance team and includes a hashed digest of the deleted objects. A sample manifest file is attached (sample-proof-of-delete-csv.txt).
- Compensating controls for scoped retention extensions (if you request >30 days):
  * Encrypted incremental backups retained for the amended window (AES-256 with KMS-wrapped keys)
  * Access logging on retention exports and strict role-based release (RBAC) + customer notification thread
  * Time-limited read-only export tokens and a notarized attestation for deletion steps after expiration

Notes / timeline: producing a tenant export + signed manifest typically takes 48–72 hours from authorization and confirmation of tenant ID and date range. If the request requires a contract amendment for a retention carveout (e.g., 90-day retention for VH-9234), Procurement and Legal will need to sign a simple addendum — that adds ~5–10 business days depending on countersignature speed.

Cost and SLA impact: scoped retention beyond the default incurs storage and processing charges; I'll share a short estimate after we confirm the exact retention window and size.

Mina — confirming we should proceed once Priya returns the tenant ID and whether Vitality requires notarization or a DocuSign-signed attestation.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
